item.title: A Review of 2019
item.description:
It’s crazy to look back and think about all of the things that has happened in my life so far. In 2009, I was in middle school. No one likes middle school. Thankfully a lot has changed since the beginning of the decade, but this year has been action-packed. So…

What happened this year?

The 2019 year alone has been a wild ride, so hopefully I can get a chance to cover a good amount of what went down.

I finished school!

I graduated from The University of Texas at Austin with a B.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering! So much of this decade has been me dreaming for this moment to happen, and now I’m left asking myself what else is next in my life. College was an experience that I’d never trade for anything. I’m super grateful for the friends that I’ve made during my four years at UT, the brutal anxieties and pressures from my classes and workload, and disappointing amount of rejections that came from finding a job as a new grad after school.

I found a job!

Working as a software engineer at JPMorgan Chase & Co. has been an a ton of fun where I can get to learn and build upon my skillset. I’m surrounded by such brilliant people that have been at the firm as long as I have, as well as people that have been around for the entire decade. I’m also grateful to be around people that are willing to help me grow and kick start my career fresh out of college. There are so many more things to achieve in my professional life, and I can’t wait to see where it gets me.

I live alone!

I’ve never had a chance to have my own sense of freedom and the feeling of independence of living by myself without any roommates. Having a roommate in college was a necessity in order to save money on rent. Now having this opportunity to have my own space, I’ve noticed that my mental health has improved a lot, and I’ve been able to really concentrate on things that are important to me. Paying a bit more for rent may suck at times, but freedom and peace of mind that I get is well worth it in my opinion.

What did you learn?

The Art of Being Alone

One of the most important things I’ve learned so far is the ability to embrace loneliness.

Having the freedom to live alone adds to this a bit, but there are days where I still don’t feel to myself because of one thing: the internet.

Everyone nowadays has a cell phone, and most likely has a means of using the internet to reach anyone they want around the world. The thought that someone can just message me in the matter of seconds about anything can be nice and refreshing sometimes, but it could also be a major distraction.

Being able to detach myself from things that connect me to other such as social media and my cell phone helps me enjoy the time that I truly get to myself. I still catch myself mindlessly scrolling on Twitter and striking countless conversations with people on Facebook Messenger, but the feeling of being in complete isolation puts me in an elevated state of mind of getting a deeper understanding of myself and embracing discomfort.

What’s next?

I have a tendency of wanting to do a lot of things, but never doing them. This includes:

  • Reading more
  • Traveling more
  • Writing more (hopefully)
  • Focusing more on my health
  • Learning new things
  • Finding new hobbies/passions

These are just things off the top of my head, but it’s probably better to have a more concise list of goals for the next year.

Read a book a month

I’ve been reading James Clear’s “Atomic Habits” for the past couple of months, and it has completely changed the way I see myself and the processes that are unconsciously happening without me knowing. For anyone looking to develop better habits and breaking the bad ones, I definitely suggest reading this!

I’ve been very attracted towards non-fiction self-improvement type books lately, so I feel like I should change it up and read something a bit different. There’s been a lot of book lists that have been releasing since the new year is coming around, so I’m have a lot to pick and choose from. I want to read a fiction book next, so I might pick up “Where the Crawdads Sing” by Delia Owens or “Little Fires Everywhere” by Celeste Ng.

Traveling more

For several years, I’ve been pretty envious of my friend Max’s travel adventures on Instagram. I’ve also grown a bit tired of always going back home for the holidays, so I figured that I won’t be accomplishing much if I’m just daydreaming about all the places I could go, when I could just go and do it.

I’ve never planned a trip before, and I’m not a very spontaneous person to just pack my bags and head into unknown territory. The danger just makes it seem twice as fun though. I told myself that I would go on a solo road trip to Colorado or New Mexico to try out skiing, but I’ll update if that actually happens. 😅

See you around soon…?

Thanks for reading, and I hope to write some more over this upcoming year. No promises though. Goals are meant to be broken.

Hope you’ve had an amazing year along with me, and it’s time to finish up the year strong. Happy New Year, and much love.

A

item.title: Long Time No See
item.description:
It’s been awhile since I’ve written anything, and I feel like now’s a good time for me to give an update as to what’s been going on so far in my life. I’m on a plane for about four hours back to Austin, so buckle up, grab a beer (or some water I guess), and enjoy the ride.

The past two and a half months have been a pretty wild ride so far, and I’ve learn a lot about engineering, start-ups, running a business, and ultimately myself.

What have you been up to?

Here’s some things that I’ve taken an interest in so far:

  • Ultimate frisbee
  • Rock climbing
  • Reading
  • Photography
  • Weightlifting
  • Fashion
  • Eating healthy
  • Investing/Personal Finance
  • Anime
  • Programming
  • Businesses, Start-ups

As you can see, this list has some pretty basic hobbies, sports, and activities. It’s mind-blowing to me that I’ve been missing out on a lot of this stuff for a good chunk of my life, and it feels like now was the right time to finally explore them! If it weren’t for being in Cambridge, I honestly have no clue what I’d be doing.

How was your internship?

My internship has taught me a lot about the software engineering world. During my time here, I got to experience what it’s like to be a full-stack software engineer using Ember.js and Ruby on Rails. I’ve never touched this sort of stuff before, so it was a good opportunity for me to learn how to make API calls, parse JSON objects, and play around with a rather large and sophistocated codebase.

The best part about my time at Ovation would have to be the brilliant and talented people that I get to work with every day. I’m not the best programmer, but I’m glad that everyone was very open to helping me grow my abilities as an engineer. Getting to talk to everyone at the office was great, and I’ll definitely miss spending time having lunch together at the table in our kitchen eating some bomb vegan bowls from a local shop down the street (Life Alive, sponsor me pls).

What’s changed?

During this summer, I was able to spend time to self-reflect to figure myself out and who I wanted to be, what my goals are, and how I want to get there.

Embracing Uncomfort was something that I’ve always struggled with for the past few years. I still often find myself having troubles with being alone. Doing things that I want to do despite having no one to tag alongside me was a big step in the right direction for me. It was perfectly okay to be alone. A bit of myself was at ease not having people around me.

I also found myself living spontaneously and just doing things without worrying too much about what’s going to happen next. A couple weeks ago my friends and I took a trip to New York City. As a small town boy from Amarillo, it’s weird finding myself in such a big city. There wasn’t much planning involved for the trip, and we just kind of went with the flow of things. There were definitely hiccups here and there, but that’s okay.

I was okay with the random Puerto Rican parade and 30 minute delay from the 7 Train from Flushing. I was okay with spending an extra 4 hours in Manhattan from missing the bus back to Boston. I was okay with getting hustled out of $25 with a friend to attend a shitty 3 hour comedy show. The last-minute trip to the Big Apple was a great time, and was definitely a time well spent.

Now let’s get down to business.

I’ve been doing things wrong for the past 3 years. I have a year left to change it.

I’ve always been the type of person to dive headfirst into whatever I’m working on without thinking what I should do first to make this a lot easier on myself in the future. I tend to skim over the details of what I’m working on and what I’m trying to learn out of it.

Basically, I feel like a copy-paste programmer.

I’ve skipped out on a lot of the details and tried forced myself to go through lots of hand-waving and head nods to get to where I am now. I am not proud of that at all. It’s time for me to fix that. I need to be okay with constantly asking HOW things work, and WHY they happen to work that way. I need to train my mind to think differently in order to become a better problem solver, and I hope to man my own ship instead of staying on cruise control. Those 10,000 hours of work aren’t going to happen on its own.

So now what?

I’m not really sure what’s next. I’ll have to think about it some more. But in the meantime, I’d love to hear what people want me to write about.

–

See you guys next time,

A

item.title: Sunday Reflections 3
item.description:
Howdy! I’m back for another week’s writing session just to recollect and see where things are so far. A lot’s happened this week, and this upcoming week will be even more hectic.

What did you do this past week?

This week was a chance for me to meet up with my fellow family and friends from Amarillo! It’s always fun for me to hear about how everyone is doing and catch up on things while I was in Austin. It’s a joy for me to just see people making little improvements day by day and trying to push themselves to be better. It’s also a blessing to see that my family is doing well, and they always welcome me with open arms when I come home. :)

What did you learn?

This week, I found out that I got offered an internship in Boston working for a start-up called Ovation! I’m super grateful for my friend Ka Tai for referring me to this internship, and I’m super excited, and honestly a very-bit nervous, to be spending my summer right in the middle of MIT and Harvard! Despite the rent being $1,200/month up there, I’m looking forward to learning as much as I can, keeping an open mind, and being willing to try new things!

What’s in your way?

I wanna say that nothing’s in my way as of right now. There’s not much on my plate as of yet, but I’m super nervous about moving super far away from Texas and working for the summer at a city where I know absolutely nobody. Eek.

Also, part of me is still wanting to hold off on buying a DSLR camera, but since I’m going to be working during the summer, I’d might as well get a camera, right? I just hope I choose the right camera and the right lenses so that I don’t regret it later.

What are you plans for next week?

This upcoming week will be pretty tight, as I have to go to the dentist later to fix a hole in my tooth (my filling came out during the semester and never got it fixed, smh), drive back to Austin to move stuff out of my apartment to prep for the move-in of my new apartment in North Campus, and fly out to Boston to start my internship!

I’ve also been holding off on prepping for technical interviews, but I hope to start when I get settled in at Boston. * fingers crossed *

Interesting thoughts or ideas?

Here’s some good reads that I’ve had in my bookmarks, or have found recently on the interwebs.

Introspect Yourself - Daniel Gross

Screw Finding Your Passion - Mark Manson (Been wanting to read his book).

Thanks for reading! I hope you guys have a wonderful week ahead, and I hope to see you here next time!

item.title: Sunday Reflections 2
item.description:
Welcome back to my second Sunday reflections! I know I skipped last week, so pls don’t hate me for it! I took a bit of time to just relax after the semester was over and splurged out on some video games, but I’ll stay consistent from here on out. I also changed a bit of my website so that the main page is now the “About” tab! Just a small little change.

What did you do this past week? (In this case, two weeks)

Over the past couple of weeks, I took some time to just relax from the axieties of school and numbed my brain with a bit of video games. After that, I had to get back into the productive mindset as I had one last internship interview with a startup company thanks to a friend’s referral. The company sounds really cool, and I feel like I can learn a lot from them if the opportunity arrises. I hear back Tuesday!!!

I’m also back home in Amarillo now after spending a good 8 hours of my Saturday driving back. The lone road trip with low-speed internet is a disaster, and having to deal with my songs on Spotify buffering every 10 minutes made it extremely annoying when I’m behind the wheel.

What did you learn?

I spent a few days working on an Amazon Alexa app that gives the cheapest flight price from Austin to Boston given a certain date. Unfortunately, I didn’t get this to work due to some limitations with Alexa and the time it took to scrape a webpage for pricing info. :( I had a pretty fun time working on it, and had an idea of making an Alexa app that tells you all of the current Free-to-Play champions for League of Legends! We’ll see if I have time for it this summer.

The majority of the work with the Alexa app was done in Javascript, so I had to take a bit of time looking over how Node.js worked. I hope I can play around with Javascript some more to get more fluent in the language so I can use it for some cool web development stuff (like the stuff on codepen.io).

What’s in your way?

Now that I’m back at home, I think a big challenge for me is to stay on top of things while I’m in the big Amarillo comfort zone. I need to start “Cracking the Coding Interview” pretty soon, as well as picking up where I left off with the books I forgot about last summer.

A friend of mine also reminded me that I should look into getting a head-start into my Operating Systems class for next fall. I think a good goal for me is to work my ass off to get an A in that class, despite it being a notoriously difficult class. I have the first couple of projects already, so it’ll only be a matter of time before I can look into it.

What are you plans for next week?

  • Spend time with friends and family, enjoy my time in Amarillo
  • Get back on the workout grind, yeet
  • Start planning out how I’m going to be studying for technical interviews
  • Read more instead of playing video games (lol, sorry homies)
  • Glance at Operating Systems stuff
  • Anxiously wait to hear back about my possible life-changing internship opportunity

Interesting thoughts or ideas?

I watched some pretty good movies after school ended like “500 Days of Summer” and “The Big Sick.” I’m a big fan of romance films, and these are definity going on my small list of favorite movies. They’re definite worth checking out.

Nothing really inspirational from me right now, but I hope everyone’s doing well and enjoys the rest of their Memorial Day weekend!

item.title: Sunday Reflections 1
item.description:
Here’s the beginning of my weekly reflections on everything that goes on in my life! I really hope that I get to keep up with writing consistently every week just to vent my thoughts on here, as well as telling my own story the more I follow through with this. The blog looks bland as of right now, but I’ll try my best to make it look a bit more presentable. Honestly. the minimalistic look that Jekyll provides me isn’t too bad in my opinion.

I’ll try template my weekly blogs to consist of of the same main questions, but this is also subject to change as well. Here it goes!

What did you do this past week?

This past week was pretty stressful with finals coming around to round out the spring semester. I’ve always had trouble managing my time when it comes to studying for two finals on the same day, but I think I did alright on both of those exams (but I definitely could’ve done better). After taking two finals on Thursday, I finally had a chance to breathe and relax a bit from the stress that school puts on me.

I’m still actively searching for internships over the summer, and I’ve been beating myself up about not being about to find anything having both the fall and spring semester to search for one. In reality, I should be progressing my career at my own pace, and if I don’t feel ready to search for an internship, I shouldn’t be looking until I feel prepared to look for one. There’s a lot of brushing up that I have to do in terms of studying for technical interviews, reviewing core fundamental programming knowledge, and getting to know myself better and building that confidence to talk about myself without bringing myself down.

What did you learn?

One thing that really hit me this week was when my roommate and I had a personal conversation about our feelings and emotional situation. There’s been a lot on my mind about where I am right now, and whether or not I’m happy with where I see myself in the near future. Long story short, I’m starting to think more about who I am, and I’m slowly learning more about the person I’m growing up to be, and a bit more about who I am as of right now (This was a bit convoluted and confusing, but please bare with me LOL).

What’s in your way?

I currently have my Jazz Appreciation final on tuesday (the very last day of finals week wtf) and haven’t put much effort into studying for it yet. I’m a pretty avid jazz guy, and I feel as though this exam will be pretty easy and straightforward - nothing like Concurrent and Distributed Systems or Vector Calculus.

I’ve also found that I’ve been holding myself back to things that I want to pursue because I sometimes don’t have the balls to do it. I’ve been thinking about starting to get serious about photography and buying a DSLR camera, but I’ve been really holding myself back from it due to the costs and whether I’ll have the time to actively continue with taking pictures. We’ll see where this goes.

What are you plans for next week?

I have a friend coming in town the day after my final, so I hope that I get to hang out, grab a drink, and enjoy some company and the beautiful city of Austin for a little bit without thinking too much about school! There’s tons of things to do here in Austin, and I’ve been missing out on some cool things such as canoeing and hiking to see some nice ass views of the city. I’ll probably head back home next week for a little bit to just spend time with family and friends in Amarillo.

Interesting thoughts or ideas?

Here’s a good ass video that I saw by Casey Neistat that really motivated me to stop with all the bullshit excuses that I give myself.

I’m a bit rusty with writing and conveying my thoughts on here, but I’ll continue to keep working on it!

Hope to see you guys back here soon.

item.title: I Only Love My LSTMs And My N-Grams - Drake Lyrics Generator
item.description:
A machine learning project to produce Drake’s lyrics and possibly write Take Care Part 2


Team Members: Julian Domingo, Karthik Konath, Alex Ma, Kyle Polansky

Github Link: https://github.com/JulianDomingo/drake_lyrics

If you would like to view our presentation for the project, click here!


Motivation

For our Data Science Laboratory class, EE 379K, we were tasked with a project to demonstrate the machine learning techniques that we have learned from the course throughout the semester. After exploring the plethora of options for our assignment, we decided to create a rap lyric generator that closely mimics the popular rap artist Drake.

One interesting idea we had in mind was to venture into ghostwriting, which is an interesting topic that consistently come up in rap culture. Many people believe that ghostwriting isn’t being a true and authentic artist if one isn’t writing their own lyrics, but many successful rappers have had reached top charts with songs that they never even wrote.

Drake has been part of the ghostwriting scene, being known for his verbal battles with Meek Mill.

For better or worse, ghostwriters are secretly being used throughout all genres of the music industry. We thought it would be cool to possibly make our own A.I. ghostwriter to recreate lyrics that could be the next club banger, as well as further understand the methods of Natural Language Processing/Generation. We will also dive deeper into machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch and Tensorlow.

Data Collection

Our project requires lyrics from songs written by Drake. In addition to raw lyrics, we save verse markers to help identify song composition. Finally we save standard metadata like the song name and album that it originated in.

We started by using a simple Spotify API search q="artist:Drake" to list all of Drake’s songs. We removed some of the extraneous punctuation to standardize the titles.

With a list of Drake’s songs, we used Beautiful Soup to scrape lyrics off MetroLryics and Genius when the lyrics couldn’t be found on MetroLryics. Our scraper is based off a sample by Ruslan Nikolaev, but expanded to support more lyrics websites and a more dynamic song list. We ended up with 139 songs using this method.

In the future, more advanced song searches could be performed for additional lyric data, such as looking for unreleased songs or ones where Drake is a featured artist. If this approch is pursued, it’s important to be careful only to select specific verses that Drake wrote and preformed.

Preprocessing

| Excuse the language |

With our dataset aquired, we ran it through a few preprocessing steps. The first is to replace all newline characters with a more visible |-| character that denotes the end of a line. This character is treated more like a word than a whitespace character as it greatly effects the song rhythm and flow.

Next up we normalized words in the lyrics. For example, the words yeah, yuh, and yea are all lexically identical. As our models focused primarily on character and word structure, we also removed most punctuation such as trailing commas and question marks. We also made all words lowercase in order to maintain uniformity when the lyrics are generated.

Finally, we noticed that a few songs were released both as a single and part of an album, and hence in our data set twice. We manually removed these duplicate songs so they don’t adversely effect the algorithm.

Now Let’s Get to the Machine Learning!

N-Gram Markov Chain Models

Overview

The first approach we used to generate Drake’s lyrics were N-Gram Markov Chains. We converted the pre-processed lyrics into order 1,2, and 3 n-grams so we would test how varying the order of the N-Gram Markov chain changes the predicted sentence. We then generated Markov Chains with the probability of changing to a particular state being proportional to the number of times the next state succeeded the previous state in the corpus. We continue advancing states until an end of verse marker is found in the next state.

Order Comparison

It seemed order 2 N-gram Markov Chains performed the best in terms of balancing creativity vs coherence and similarity to Drake’s own lyrics. When we moved to order 3 chains, lyrics were essentially just being copied from songs completely, while order 1 chains lacked the coherence and similarity that we desired. However, considering that every word choice was randomly based off only the previous one for order 1 chains, the results were surprisingly good.

LSTM RNNs (Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Nets)

Overview

The other approach we used to generate lyrics was through a RNN, but specifically an LSTM RNN. The primary difference in the LSTM is its inherent ability to learn long-term dependencies in the data, whereas a regular RNN is severely limited in this regard.

This prominent difference is due to the increased complexity of the network’s update equation:

As seen above, a regular RNN simply contains repeating, single tanh layers.

On the other hand, LSTM layers contain four, interacting neural network layers of point-wise operations (i.e. vector addition), concatenation, and copying of vectors to different locations within each network cell.

Character-Level vs. Word-Level Models

We trained two types of LSTM RNNs: one models the data at a character level, predicting the subsequent character given a pre-specified input sequence; the other models the data at a word level, predicting the subsequent word given a pre-specified input sequence. This prediction is repeatedly performed until the specified character or word length threshold is reached.

Softmax Classifier (Cross-Entropy Loss)

We run the same training process for both the character-level and word-level RNN: given an input sequence (i.e. “The sky is”), we one-hot encode each character (or word) into individual vectors, then feed each into the RNN iteratively. This ultimately produces a sequence of n-dimensional output vectors (one for each character or word in the input sequence), containing confidence scores the RNN assigns for the subsequent character or word in the sequence:

This confidence score assignment is repeated continuously until the scores converge, determined through the LSTM’s backpropagation algorithm which determines what directions the LSTM should adjust the network weights to. Ultimately, this increases the confidence of the “expected” subsequent character or word. In our project’s case, we use mini-batch gradient descent to accomplish this goal. Compared to stochastic gradient descent and batch gradient descent, mini-batch succeeds in its ability to more quickly converge the confidence scores, while its increased frequency in updating the model’s states allows computational efficiency due to not having all training data in memory. This helped tremendously in improving our model’s predictive capabilities, especially due to our time constraints (Tuesday team rip).

Perplexity Scoring

The metric we use to determine the “correctness” of our model’s predictions is through the perplexity function, shown below:

where ptargeti is the probability of character or word i occurring as the prediction. The character-level RNN converged to a lower perplexity score in comparison to the word-level RNN, shown below:

Character-Level Model

For the character-level model, the RNN progressively begins to understand grammatical syntax, and at epoch 50, it begins to model internal rhyming. We concluded that the character-level RNN ended up performing significantly better after a long period of training due to the smaller size of our training corpus - with more data to train on, the word-level model would likely perform at a similar level as the character-level RNN.

Fun Facts

Our dataset contains 75,121 words, with only 5908 unique words. The top 10 most common words are:

Word Count

It’s interesting that many of the most commonly used words are quite short. In fact, nearly 73% of our dataset is composed of words that are 4 characters or less. We can hypothesize that Drake’s structure is very simple and contains many link words.

Looking at the most common bigrams, we see that Drake commonly talks about himself and someone else “you” quite frequently in his music. The trigrams don’t reveal a whole lot about the dataset in general, but rather expose patterns that are very common in his songs. For example, the song Versace has the trigram ‘versace’, ‘versace’, ‘versace’ 72 times in the song.

Conclusion

To conclude, we created a rap lyric generator that closely mimics rap artist Drake by using a LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) neural net by scraping for his lyrics from sites such as Genius and MetroLyrics. We also explored the options of using Markov Chains to generate lyrics that could possibly be more coherent.

In the future, we hope to look deeper into implementing a rhyming scheme, and to have the model generate verses and hooks to create its own rap song. In general, this model and technique could be applied to different music artists and could be expanded to create lyrics certain genres. We found that this Stanford research paper could help us achieve that goal.
